approach:
Add one lexical gate step, `check_environment_reach(reading)`, in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs next to `check_code_survey` (3910), registered as one `step!` line right after `step!(check_outcome_state(reading, request));` (3248). It returns Ok when capability is None or a question is set; nothing else gates it, so a reading with no deliverables is still checked (reading.rs:2772 shows a capability reading may list none). Triggers: (A) a Create/Modify deliverable under `.github/workflows/`; (B) a host action in a Behavior criterion; (C) a records or history source in a Behavior criterion or the summary. Content criteria, assumptions, out_of_scope and the request are never scanned, so the `Environment:` repair text cannot trigger its own check. A triggered reading needs one `Environment:` assumption with a site word, a permission word and a data word; for B, a no/without/missing-origin case only when the assumption names a local-type site (local, producer, snapshot, checkout, copy); for C, a source word plus a counted figure or a reachable data/doc file path. Grammar (revised to fit the fixtures): text is tokenised; backticked spans are kept for command forms (`git push|fetch|clone|pull|remote`, `gh pr|api|run|auth|workflow|release|issue`) and for `athena/records`, and every other backticked span is a break marker; bare tokens containing `/`, `_`, `::` or an interior `.` become break markers (so `gh/early.rs`, `parse_remote`, 'push/pull-request/gh' never match); the rest is lowercased and split on non-alphanumerics. Phrase windows never cross a break. B phrases: `git`+push/fetch/clone/pull/remote; `gh`+command word; a push verb with origin/remote/upstream/branch(es)/ref(s) within 4 words on EITHER side (active and passive); fetch/clone/pull verbs with origin/remote/upstream within 3 words after (not `pull request`); `pull request(s)` with open/create/raise/submit/merge/push forms within 3 words on EITHER side (passive 'A pull request is opened'). C phrases: job records, job history, commit history, git history, git log, records branch, `athena/records` (bare or backticked), with one of from/use/uses/using/read/reads/counts/measures/replays/queries/parses/scans in the 3 words before. 'in' and 'reading' are not verbs, so writes ('written in the records branch') and this job's own criterion 4 ('a reading citing job records') do not trigger. The rule line in READING_RULES, the CHANGELOG entry, the doc comment (root cause: no step asking who performs each action, where, with what permissions, and what data it reaches; jobs 20261024-220048-engm, 20261025-070538-8ra0, 20261025-034247-nm0k) and corpus cases follow. The 8% share is declared as an unmeasured estimate with its basis.

Fixture map (rule that fires; the producer pins each as a test): 'Athena pushes the job branch to origin' -> B push verb + branch/origin after (refuse). 'The job branch is pushed to the remote' -> B push verb, branch 2 words before (refuse). 'A pull request is opened on the remote' -> B pull request + opened 2 after (refuse). 'The pull request is opened with `gh pr create`' -> B backtick command and pull-request rule (refuse). 'The history check reads the job records on the records branch' -> C, 'reads' 2 words before 'job records' (refuse without a figure). 'Use the figures from job records and history' (summary) -> C, 'from' adjacent (refuse). 'The record is written in the records branch' -> no verb in the 3 words before (accept). 'fixed where it originates' -> word 'originates' is not 'origin' (accept). 'crates/athena-core/src/gh/early.rs', `parse_remote`, 'push/pull-request/gh' -> break markers (accept). 'entries are pushed onto the list', 'Vec push', 'pushdown', 'remotely', 'ghost' -> no target or other word (accept). This job's criteria 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 texts -> no phrase fires (accept).

decisions.choice: Scan Behavior criteria for host actions and records sources, the summary for records sources only, and the deliverable list for workflows. Do not scan Content criteria, assumptions, out_of_scope or the request.
decisions.reason: A Behavior criterion is the one that must be run, so that is where an action or measurement is assigned (CriterionKind has only Content and Behavior). A workflow deliverable is a real CI assignment. The summary is read for C only because job nm0k cited records in its summary. Skipping assumptions keeps the repair text from triggering its own check.

rejected.option: Scan every criterion with bare-word triggers
rejected.why: Fires on gh/early.rs, parse_remote and 'entries are pushed onto the list'.
A request can mention push without the reading assigning it.

decisions.choice: Make the grammar match the fixtures (answers finding 1). Passive and active forms are both matched: push verb with a target within 4 words on either side; `pull request(s)` with an open/create/raise/submit/merge/push verb within 3 words on either side. Backticked spans are scanned for command forms (`git push|fetch|clone|pull|remote`, `gh pr|api|run|auth|workflow|release|issue`) and for `athena/records`; every other backticked span, and every bare token with `/`, `_`, `::` or an interior `.`, becomes a break marker. The `athena/records` word is matched bare and in backticks. The source verbs are from, use, uses, using, read, reads, counts, measures, replays, queries, parses, scans. 'reading' is not a verb.
decisions.reason: Each refuse fixture is traced to a rule in the fixture map above, so the demonstrations can show the refusals. Commands are written in backticks, so dropping them would lose the real signal. Marking path and identifier tokens as breaks keeps gh/early.rs, parse_remote and this job's slash-joined 'push/pull-request/gh' from matching. Adding 'read/reads' catches the engm shape, and leaving out 'reading' keeps this job's criterion 4 an accept fixture.

rejected.why: Loses `gh pr create` and `git push`, the usual place a command is written.

rejected.option: Whole-token match on push, origin, remote, gh
rejected.why: Splitting paths and identifiers yields those words.

decisions.choice: Source verbs exclude 'in' (answers finding 4). An accept fixture 'The record is written in the records branch' shows a write does not trigger.
decisions.reason: 'in' also fits writes; the class is reads and measurements of data the site may not reach.

rejected.why: Demands quoted figures for a write.

decisions.choice: The no-origin case is required only when the Environment assumption names a local-type site (local, producer, snapshot, checkout, copy). It is satisfied by the word 'origin' with one of no, without, missing, absent, none, non, always, lacks. An assumption naming only a CI, runner, workflow or GitHub site needs no such case (answers finding 2).
decisions.reason: A CI job always has an origin; the 8ra0 gap was a local or producer run with no origin or a non-GitHub origin. 'always' lets a local site state that its origin is always present.

rejected.option: Require a no-origin case for every host action
rejected.why: Forces filler when the site is CI.

decisions.choice: Reachable-file alternative for C: a raw token that contains `/`, has an extension in md, json, jsonl, csv or txt, and does not start with records/ or athena/records. Code and config extensions (rs, toml, yml) are not accepted. Existence is left to `check_reading_references`, which scans assumptions (reading.rs:3148-3151) and refuses a path whose top directory is in the snapshot (or in KNOWN_TOP_DIRS) and that does not exist and is not created. A path under another top directory is not verified; the doc comment states this limit (answers finding 3).
decisions.reason: Ties the file to data and docs, not source code, and reuses the existing existence check instead of passing repo_files into the new one.

rejected.option: Any file with an allowed extension, including .rs
rejected.why: crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs would satisfy a records-figure rule.

rejected.option: Pass repo_files into the new check

decisions.choice: Counted figure for C: 1 to 5 digits directly before job(s), reading(s), commit(s), record(s), run(s), plan(s), introspection(s), attempt(s), case(s) or percent, or digits directly before `%`; it must sit in the same Environment assumption as a source word (records, history, log, logs, commits, branch). refs, branches and files are not counted nouns.
decisions.reason: A year ('sees main as of 2026') or a count of refs is not a quoted records figure.

decisions.choice: No empty-deliverable gate: return Ok only when capability is None or a question is set (answers finding 5; replaces the earlier gate).
decisions.reason: A capability reading may list no deliverables (only a retry is refused for that, reading.rs:2772) and still assign a measurement from job records, the engm and nm0k class. Dropping the gate removes a limit instead of documenting one. The workflow trigger needs a deliverable anyway.

rejected.why: Skips measurement-only readings, which are part of the class.

decisions.choice: Place `step!(check_environment_reach(reading));` directly after `check_outcome_state`. Workflow corpus cases carry the Create deliverable and a Content criterion naming it, and a request that names no governance path.
decisions.reason: `check_governance_coverage` (3326-3331) refuses an unnamed workflow deliverable first. After outcome_state keeps the test `check_outcome_state_doc_names_root_cause_and_scope` (7725) and the corpus anchor `step!(check_reading_references(` unchanged.

rejected.why: Breaks the ordering that test pins.

decisions.choice: Declare 'expected 8% of newly refused readings' as an estimate that was not measured, with its basis: no records in the snapshot to replay; 11 lines of HISTORY.txt name `.github/workflows` (about 5% of 200 commits); the host-action and records triggers add a small allowance. The CHANGELOG entry is cut out (from the line holding 'no step asking who performs each action' to the next line starting `- ` or `#`) before the needles are asserted. The doc comment is cut at `pub fn check_environment_reach`, as `code_survey_refusal_is_declared_intended` does (reading.rs:9142).
decisions.reason: The criterion text fixes 8%. Slicing stops older entries that already hold 'higher refusal rate is intended' from satisfying the test.

decisions.choice: The completeness test is a fixed word list: site (ci, runner, workflow, producer, snapshot, local, host, github, reader, planner, verifier, critic), permission (read, reads, write, writes, writable, readonly, permission, permissions), data (refs, ref, branch, branches, records, history, files, repo, repository, checkout, data, commits, logs, figures, origin, remote). No schema, table, data file, prompt file or model call. The label `Environment:` matches after trim, in any case. Word lists use only CI and host vocabulary (the boundary scan in xtask/tests/policy.rs bans some words, for example 'remote session'; the doc comment avoids them).
decisions.reason: No record schema change (Reading is deny_unknown_fields), no model call, and the reader brief sits outside the budgeted prompt sets, so the budget lines in docs/system-facts.md do not move.

rejected.option: Add an `environment` field or a capabilities table file
rejected.why: Changes the record schema or adds a data file; both are out of scope.

rejected.option: Judge the assumption with a model call
rejected.why: Adds cost and nondeterminism to a gate that runs no model, and cannot be pinned in the corpus.

risks.risk: Lexical triggers miss an action described in other words, or catch a prose mention in a Behavior criterion. The 8% share is an unmeasured estimate.
risks.mitigation: Triggers are limited to Behavior criteria, the summary for records sources, and workflow deliverables. They need a verb-plus-target phrase and skip path, identifier and non-command backticked tokens. The fixture map, accept tests and corpus cases pin both sides, including this job's own criteria. The doc comment and CHANGELOG label 8% as an estimate with its basis.

risks.risk: This job's own accepted summary may differ from the text in the brief and hold a records phrase, so it would be newly refused.
risks.mitigation: The summary is scanned for records sources only and needs a source verb before the phrase. The summary text in the brief ('unreachable records', 'job' ids) has no phrase, and a test pins it as an accept fixture. Lists are tuned by adding corpus cases, not by weakening the check.

risks.risk: The word lists can be met by a wrong sentence.
risks.mitigation: The check makes the reader state site, permission and data; the doc says it is lexical, as for the `Code survey:` rule. The refusal text names what is missing. The figure rule needs a counted noun and the file rule excludes records paths and code files.

risks.risk: Existing tests or fixtures that accept workflow-deliverable or action-bearing readings fail once the step exists.
risks.mitigation: Plan step 4 edits the two known tests; the workspace run finds any other, which gets an `Environment:` assumption.

risks.risk: A corpus refuse case is refused by an earlier check (criteria evidence, governance, references) and does not exercise the new step.
risks.mitigation: Workflow cases include a criterion naming the workflow path and a request that names no governance path; accept cases use only docs/guide.md and docs/design/roadmap.md from `repo_files()`; the producer checks each refuse case names `check_environment_reach` and rewrites the Behavior sentence as a `Run ...` form if `check_criteria_evidence` objects.

risks.risk: The rule line exceeds the 220-byte cap or the section bound in briefs.rs.
risks.mitigation: The draft is about 200 bytes with the `- ` prefix; the producer measures it and sets the section bound just above the measured size.

risks.risk: New code or comment text trips the boundary scan or the personal-data allow-list.
risks.mitigation: Use CI and host vocabulary only, avoid the banned phrases (for example 'remote session') and write no email-like text; the workspace run includes the scan.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests `environment_reach_*` in reading.rs `mod tests`, calling `refusing_check` (3226) and `check_environment_reach` directly. Guards: capability set, no question. Refuse, with no `Environment:` assumption: (i) Create `.github/workflows/lint.yml` plus a Content criterion naming it (so governance passes); (ii) one Behavior criterion each: 'Athena pushes the job branch to origin', 'The job branch is pushed to the remote', 'A pull request is opened on the remote', 'The pull request is opened with `gh pr create`', and a bare `git push` backtick; the refusing check name is `check_environment_reach` and the error starts 'the reading was refused because'. Accept: the same readings with 'Environment: the CI job has write permission to refs on the GitHub origin' for the CI-site cases; for a local-site case ('the local Athena working copy has write access to the repo; with no origin or a non-GitHub origin it skips the push; with a GitHub origin it can push refs') `refusing_check` returns None. Also: an assumption missing the permission word is refused and the error names 'permissions'; a local-site assumption without the no-origin case is refused; a CI-site assumption without it is accepted (finding 2); the label matches after trim and in any case, and an assumption that only mentions the word 'environment' does not count; a Delete of a workflow does not trigger.
demonstrations.observes: A workflow deliverable, or a push, pull-request or gh action in a Behavior criterion, without a complete `Environment:` assumption is refused by `check_environment_reach`; with one, `refusing_check` gives None.
demonstrations.fails_without: With the `step!` line removed, `refusing_check` returns None for the refused readings and the check-name assertions fail. With the label or word lists wrong, the accept assertions fail.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests `environment_reach_source_*` in reading.rs, each also run through `refusing_check` to assert the refusing check's name. Three readings shaped like the three jobs. (engm) a code-class reading with a `Code survey:` assumption naming a crates/ path (so `check_code_survey` passes) and the Behavior criterion 'The history check reads the job records on the records branch': refused with no Environment assumption; refused with a site, permission and data assumption that quotes no figure and lists no file (error says to quote figures inline or name a reachable file); accepted with 'Environment: the CI job has read-only access to contents and cannot write the records branch; it sees 3 jobs and 12 readings'. (8ra0) the push/origin/pull-request reading of criterion 3, accepted only with a complete assumption. (nm0k) a docs reading whose summary says 'Use the figures from job records and history': refused; accepted when the assumption quotes '3 jobs' or '40%'; accepted when it lists `docs/design/roadmap.md`; refused when the only file is `records/foo.json`, `athena/records/x.json` or `crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs`; refused when the only number is a year ('sees main as of 2026'). A reading with no deliverables and a records-source Behavior criterion is refused. A loop covers every phrase (job records, job history, commit history, git history, git log, records branch, athena/records bare and in backticks), each with a source verb. A source phrase without a verb ('a reading citing job records') and 'written in the records branch' are not triggers.
demonstrations.observes: A reading that cites records or history as a source is refused unless figures are quoted inline next to a counted noun or a reachable data or doc file is listed, and is accepted when they are. Three differently shaped readings are covered, so the class is tested.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the step, `refusing_check` returns None for the refused readings and the name assertions fail. Without the figure and file rule, the 'complete but nothing quoted', bare-year and records-only-file readings are wrongly accepted.

demonstrations.method: Plan step 4 adds cases to `reading_check_cases()` (refusal_corpus.rs:668) using `case(..)` and `base_reading` (exist, 186 and 117). Refuse, `Expected::Refuse("check_environment_reach")`: environment-ci-workflow-without-an-environment (Create `.github/workflows/lint.yml` plus a Content criterion naming it), environment-host-action-without-an-environment (Behavior criterion 'Athena pushes the job branch to origin'), environment-records-source-without-figures (Behavior criterion 'The history check reads the job records on the records branch'), environment-records-source-with-a-bare-year (Environment names only a year). Accept: environment-ci-workflow-with-an-environment, environment-host-action-with-origin-cases, environment-records-source-with-quoted-figures, environment-records-source-with-a-reachable-file (lists docs/design/roadmap.md, which is in `repo_files()`), environment-trigger-words-only-inside-other-words (a dash-bullet request naming push to origin, which becomes Content criteria, plus a Behavior criterion with 'originates', a gh/early.rs path, `parse_remote`, 'entries are pushed onto the list', a Vec push), environment-gh-module-path-only. The refuse cases are kept separate from governance, outcome-state and references refusals by having the workflow deliverable named in a criterion and the request name no governance path. Add `environment_reach_refusal_is_declared_intended`, modelled on `design_existing_code_refusal_is_declared_intended` (1102). Input forms (existing ids read in the file: code-reading-without-a-survey 689, code-reading-with-a-survey 700, design-reading-without-existing-code 738, request-names-a-governance-file-the-reading-ignores 772, delivery-request-naming-a-workflow-fails-governance-first 393, full-deliverable-path 802, boundary-word-in-a-deliverable-path 890): workflow deliverable Create/Modify -> the two workflow cases; Delete -> unit test only, because the governance check's behavior for a deleted workflow was not read; push, pull-request and gh phrases -> host-action cases; records source with a figure, a file, a year -> the three records cases; slash-joined, path and identifier tokens, words inside other words -> the two accept cases; dash bullets -> the trigger-words case (the request is a dash bullet list); star and numbered bullets reach the gate only as Content criteria through `base_reading`, which the check does not scan, and are covered by the existing bullet cases (star-bullets 542, numbered-dot-parts 554). New `INPUT_FORMS` tags ci-workflow-deliverable, host-action-criterion, records-source-citation, environment-assumption, trigger-word-inside-other-word (length 23 to 28), each carried by a case. I have not run the suite and cite no result.
demonstrations.observes: Each case gets its expected outcome, and `every_acceptance_check_has_a_refusing_corpus_case` (1061) and `corpus_covers_the_listed_input_forms` (998) pass because a case refuses with `check_environment_reach` and every tag is carried.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests `environment_reach_accepts_*` in reading.rs, plus the corpus accept cases. A plain docs reading (`governed_reading(&["docs/x.md"], &["docs/x.md exists"], &[])`) passes `check_environment_reach` and `refusing_check` returns None. Accepted with no `Environment:`: Content criteria naming push, origin, gh/early.rs, parse_remote, 'the history of the page'; Behavior criteria containing only 'fixed where it originates', 'ghost', 'pushdown', 'remotely', 'Vec push', 'entries are pushed onto the list', 'The record is written in the records branch'; this job's own criteria 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7 texts and its summary text, copied from the brief; a push phrase in an assumption or in out_of_scope only; a decline (capability None); a reading with a question. The 8% estimate is pinned by the criterion 1 and 5 declaration tests.
demonstrations.observes: Docs-only readings and readings without an assigned action or a records source are accepted. Words in paths, identifiers, Content criteria and other words do not trigger.
demonstrations.fails_without: With substring or bare-token triggers, 'originates', gh/early.rs and parse_remote are refused and the accept tests fail. Without the capability and question guards, the decline and question readings are refused.

demonstrations.method: Run `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` and `cargo test --workspace` as three separate commands. The full run is needed because `check_reading_text` (reading.rs:4128) is shared by the steward, the CLI check-reading command, run/tests.rs and drain.rs, and because the workspace tests include the boundary scan and the budgets test. A fixture elsewhere that the new rule refuses is found only by the run. Any such fixture gets an `Environment:` assumption; the check is never weakened.
